factual_problem: Not wrong at ISC2 CC level: in NIST RMF the authorizing official accepts residual risk after the controls have been assessed. Minor nuance: residual risk is still an estimate after verification, and some frameworks (ISO 27005-style treatment plans) record provisional acceptance at planning time. The 'forecast vs shown' framing slightly overstates this. Acceptable for CC.
reason: Without any hint, three of the five steps are already clear from the item wording. Identify comes first because you have to name the asset, threat and vulnerability before anything else. Assess comes next because you cannot rank a risk you have not described. Choose comes before Apply because you cannot apply a control you have not picked. The one real decision is Apply/verify versus Document residual/accept. The trap is the word 'accept' inside the Choose item, which can pull 'formally accepted' up to sit right after Choose, as documenting the decision. This hint settles that decision with wording alone. 'Put their name to' / 'signature' maps onto 'have it formally accepted'. 'Shown' / 'what the work has been shown to leave behind' maps onto 'Apply the control and verify it actually works'. 'The signature only carries weight once that has been shown' is a direct ordering rule: acceptance comes after verification. The rhetorical either/or answers itself. The second option is the one the last sentence endorses, so you do not need to understand residual risk to choose it. Someone who has never heard the term can still put Document after Apply by matching sign to formally accepted and shown to verify. It does touch the concept (residual = what is left after controls are actually in place). But the final sentence turns that concept into a ready-made sequencing rule, which takes it beyond 'stating the defining distinction'. Pulling it down to MED would only be justified if learners already put 'Document' last as a closing step anyway. That is plausible, but the 'accept' lure in the Choose item makes it unreliable. Fix: drop the final sentence and the loaded either/or. Ask instead what 'residual' risk is the residue of (answer: the controls as they actually exist), so the learner has to link that to the steps themselves.
